rows.question: Can I resit an exam I already passed to get a higher grade?
rows.answer: You cannot resit an exam you already passed to get a higher grade. According to [1], a resit is allowed for both passed and failed units of education, but it is not possible to resit an exam you have already passed. The most recent mark will apply in the event of a resit, so even if you resit an exam you passed, the new result will be the same as the original mark.

rows.question: Is a final mark of 5.45 a pass?
rows.answer: According to Article 3.6 of the General programme rule [1], a final mark between 5 and 6 will be rounded to the nearest whole number. Since 5.45 is below 5.50, it will be rounded down. Therefore, a final mark of 5.45 is not a pass, as it is rounded down to 5, which is below the required mark of 6.

rows.question: When am I allowed to start my Master Project AI?
rows.answer: You are allowed to start your Master Project AI after having successfully completed 60 ECTS (in total) of the MSc Artificial Intelligence, as stated in [3]. This typically occurs after the first year of the program, which starts on 1 September, as mentioned in [2]. The Master Project AI marks the end of the Master program in Artificial Intelligence, and its start is closely tied to the completion of the required 60 ECTS.

rows.question: How many EC is the Master Project AI?
rows.answer: The Master Project AI is worth 30 EC (30 ECTS credits), as stated in the course facts [1]. This is the total number of credits allocated to the course.

rows.question: Can I redo the Evolutionary Computing programming assignment if I fail it?
rows.answer: You cannot redo the programming assignment, as stated in [1]: "No resit is possible for the programming assignment."

rows.question: If I pass the Evolutionary Computing exam but fail the assignment, do I lose my exam grade?
rows.answer: You will keep the grade of the passed component for next year or later, but you will need to pass the course by getting a good grade (> 5.5) for the missing component and using the old grade in the averaging formula [1].

rows.question: How is Deep Learning graded?
rows.answer: According to the course-specific source [1], the Deep Learning course (XM_0083) is graded with a final exam (50%) and practical assignments (50%). The final exam must be passed with a sufficient grade (equivalent to a grade of 5.5 or higher).

rows.question: Who coordinates the Evolutionary Computing course?
rows.answer: The course is coordinated by prof. dr. A.E. Eiben, as stated in the course facts [3].

rows.question: I already completed Advanced Machine Learning. Can I take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning?
rows.answer: You cannot take Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning as it is a level 400 course, and you have already completed Advanced Machine Learning, which is likely a level 300 course. [1] states that the course is level 400, and there is no indication that students can take it after completing a lower-level course.

rows.question: What is the deadline to request an extra exam opportunity, and who qualifies?
rows.answer: You must submit a request for an extra examination opportunity to the Examination Board no later than 15 July. According to Article 4 of the Teaching and Examination Regulations, this provision excludes the practical exercises and the final project, and is only possible for students who have completed all but one unit of education to meet the requirements of the degree, and have failed the examination during all the previously offered attempts unless participation in an examination was not possible for compelling reasons. [1]

rows.question: How long after an exam can I inspect my graded work?
rows.answer: You can inspect your graded work within twenty working days after the announcement of the results of a written examination, but at least ten working days before the resit opportunity for that examination. [1] This period applies to all written examinations, regardless of the course or type of exam.

rows.question: How long does an examiner have to grade a written exam?
rows.answer: According to Article 3.4 of the Artificial Intelligence TER 2026-2027, the examiner determines the result of a written examination within fifteen working days.

rows.question: I have a CS bachelor. Should I take Cognitive Psychology and its Applications or Skills for AI?
rows.answer: You should take Cognitive Psychology and its Applications, as students with an Artificial Intelligence/Computer Science bachelor degree are required to choose this course [1].
